objects.description: Abstract callback/adapter class used by Yojimbo clients and servers. Users subclass Adapter to provide an Allocator implementation, a MessageFactory instance, and optional loopback packet handling and server client connect/disconnect callbacks. The default CreateAllocator uses YOJIMBO_NEW with TLSF_Allocator; CreateMessageFactory and loopback methods assert by default and must be overridden for actual use.
Enumeration of address kinds used by yojimbo::Address to distinguish between invalid/none, IPv4, and IPv6 addresses.

Represents an IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) and port. Stores type, address bytes (union of IPv4/IPv6), and port; provides constructors from numeric fields or strings, accessors, classification helpers, string conversion, and validity checks.

objects.description: Opaque handle type used by TLSF_Allocator to refer to an underlying TLSF allocator instance. It is a void* alias; lifetime is managed by TLSF_Allocator and the external TLSF implementation.

Abstract base class defining the allocation interface used by Yojimbo. Derived allocators must implement Allocate and Free and should call TrackAlloc/TrackFree (in debug builds) and SetErrorLevel on failure. Not thread-safe. Instances are owned by user code; make sure all allocations are freed before destruction.

Concrete Allocator that delegates to malloc/free. Suitable general-purpose allocator. In debug builds, allocation tracking occurs via base class helpers. Ensure all allocated memory is freed before destruction.

Allocator implementation backed by the external TLSF algorithm. Requires a caller-provided memory block that must outlive the allocator; the allocator does not own the backing memory. Optimized for multiple heaps and fast allocation. In debug builds, will report leaks on destruction.
Debug-only record describing a single tracked allocation: size, source file, and line. Used in YOJIMBO_DEBUG_MEMORY_LEAKS builds for leak detection. Not present in release builds.
Enumeration of allocator error states. ALLOCATOR_ERROR_NONE indicates success; ALLOCATOR_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY indicates an allocation failure. Used by Allocator to report status.

Abstract base class providing common client functionality for Yojimbo client implementations. Manages configuration, allocators, message factory, connection, network simulation, and packet processing hooks. Ownership: holds pointers to Connection, MessageFactory, and NetworkSimulator used during a connection lifecycle.

Abstract base server implementation in the yojimbo namespace that provides common server functionality (lifecycle, message allocation and flow, network simulation hooks, per-client allocators and connections). It inherits from ServerInterface and requires derived classes to implement packet transmit/process functions. Construction requires an Allocator, ClientServerConfig, Adapter, and initial time.

objects.description: Forward-declared C struct representing a reliable transport endpoint used per client. Definition is not present in this header; details are unknown here.

Forward declaration of the yojimbo memory Allocator type. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; no definition here. Used by BitArray for allocation and deallocation. Details and interface are defined elsewhere.

A simple dynamic bit array storing bits in a heap-allocated array of 64-bit words. Requires an external yojimbo::Allocator to allocate and free its storage. Provides operations to clear all bits, set/clear an individual bit, query a bit, and get the total bit count. Copy construction and assignment are declared private and not defined, effectively making the class non-copyable. Destruction frees the backing memory via the provided allocator. Note: size must be > 0; m_bytes is computed to cover size bits, but the computation multiplies word count by 8, implying bytes rather than 64-bit words—this matches allocation size in bytes. All bits are initialized to zero in the constructor via Clear().

Packet-scoped data container for a single channel. Encapsulates either a set of messages (MessageData) or a block transfer fragment (BlockData) along with flags describing how to interpret the union. Provides Initialize/Free and (de)serialization helpers; actual message and block types are provided by the MessageFactory and ChannelConfig. Ownership of messages/blocks referenced here is external; Free uses the factory to release them.
Enumeration of per-channel counter indices used for telemetry/stats (messages sent/received and count of counters). Typically used to index Channel::m_counters and via Channel::GetCounter.
Error states a channel can be in. Used by Channel to report and propagate errors to connections, influencing client/server behavior (eg. disconnect on desync).

Abstract base class providing the interface and core state for a message channel over a connection. Derived classes implement specific reliability/ordering semantics, queueing, packetization (GetPacketData/ProcessPacketData), and ack handling. Manages counters and error state. Constructor requires allocator, message factory, channel config, index, and initial time.

Concrete client class within the yojimbo namespace that implements a network client on top of BaseClient. Manages connection lifecycle (connect, disconnect), packet send/receive, time advancement, loopback mode, and integrates with an underlying netcode_client_t. Fields include configuration, underlying netcode client pointer, addresses, and the client ID.

Enumeration of client lifecycle states used by the Yojimbo networking client. Values indicate error, disconnected, connecting, and connected. Primarily used for status queries and control flow.

Abstract interface defining the operations for a Yojimbo client implementation. Provides lifecycle control (connect/disconnect), networking I/O (send/receive), time advancement, message creation and transfer, block allocation/attachment, and loopback support. It is an interface only (pure virtual); concrete clients implement these methods. Notes: ownership and construction are external; no direct constructors here.
Enumeration selecting the reliability/ordering mode for a message channel: reliable-ordered or unreliable-unordered.
Per-channel configuration controlling reliability type, queue sizes, budgets, block handling, and resend timings for a message channel.
Configures global connection parameters and holds an array of per-channel ChannelConfig entries. Depends on MaxChannels constant from yojimbo_constants.h.
Extends ConnectionConfig with shared client/server tuning: protocol/versioning, memory budgets, optional network simulator controls, fragmentation parameters, buffer sizes, and RTT smoothing.

High-level endpoint that sends and receives Message objects over multiple Channel instances as configured by ConnectionConfig. Manages message queuing, packet generation/processing, ACK handling, and tracks an error level.

Abstract base class for reference-counted, serializable messages exchanged over Yojimbo connections. Provides ID/type, block-message flag, refcount acquire/release, and pure-virtual serialize methods for read/write/measure. Must be created and released via MessageFactory to ensure correct lifetime management.

Concrete message type that can carry an attached binary block. Manages allocation and freeing of the block through a provided Allocator. Provides accessors for block pointer and size. Serialization of the block payload occurs externally (see SerializeMessageBlock).
Enumeration of error states for MessageFactory. Indicates success or failure to allocate a message.

objects.definition:
namespace yojimbo
{
    /**
        Network information for a connection.
        Contains statistics like round trip time (RTT), packet loss %, bandwidth estimates, number of packets sent, received and acked.
     */

    struct NetworkInfo
    {
        float RTT;                                  ///< Round trip time estimate (milliseconds). Exponentially smoothed average tracking most recent RTT value.
        float minRTT;                               ///< Minimum RTT seen over the last n samples (see rtt_history_size in reliable config). This is a more stable and accurate RTT value under typical Wi-Fi jitter.
        float maxRTT;                               ///< Maximum RTT seen over the last n samples. 
        float averageRTT;                           ///< Average RTT seen over the last n samples.
        float averageJitter;                        ///< Average jitter relative to min RTT over the last n samples.
        float maxJitter;                            ///< Max jitter relative to min RTT seen over the last n samples.
        float stddevJitter;                         ///< One standard deviation of jitter relative to average RTT over the last n samples.
        float packetLoss;                           ///< Packet loss percent.
        float sentBandwidth;                        ///< Sent bandwidth (kbps).
        float receivedBandwidth;                    ///< Received bandwidth (kbps).
        float ackedBandwidth;                       ///< Acked bandwidth (kbps).
        uint64_t numPacketsSent;                    ///< Number of packets sent.
        uint64_t numPacketsReceived;                ///< Number of packets received.
        uint64_t numPacketsAcked;                   ///< Number of packets acked.
    };
}
objects.description: POD struct defined in the yojimbo namespace that aggregates connection telemetry: RTT statistics, jitter metrics, packet loss percentage, bandwidth estimates, and packet counters. Intended for read-only reporting of current/aggregated link health; no behavior or constructors are defined in this header.

Network conditions simulator for testing: introduces latency, jitter, packet loss, and duplicates on packet send. Owns buffered packet copies and delivers them after simulated delay. Construct with an Allocator, capacity, and initial time; advance time regularly. Free received packet data with the allocator returned by GetAllocator.

A reliable, ordered channel implementation that guarantees in-order delivery of messages. Handles message queuing, per-message acks, and special handling for large block-attached messages via fragmentation and reassembly.

Abstract base class for objects that can serialize themselves to/from Yojimbo bit streams. It declares pure-virtual overloads of SerializeInternal for ReadStream, WriteStream, and MeasureStream. Derived classes are expected to implement these via the YOJIMBO_VIRTUAL_SERIALIZE_FUNCTIONS macro that forwards to a templated Serialize method. Destructor is virtual. Forward-declared stream types are referenced but not defined in this header.

Concrete server implementation in the yojimbo namespace deriving from BaseServer. Manages a netcode_server_t instance, binding address, client connect/disconnect, sending/receiving packets, loopback clients, and time advancement. Construction requires allocator, private key, listen address, configuration, adapter, and initial time. Destruction likely stops server and releases resources, but exact semantics are defined in the implementation, not in this header.

Abstract server-side interface for the Yojimbo networking library. It defines the operations a server must implement to manage clients, send/receive messages and packets, allocate/free message-related memory, query connection state and stats, and support loopback clients. This header only declares the interface; concrete behavior is provided by implementations elsewhere. Note: GetClientUserData is declared but not pure-virtual, implying an out-of-line definition not shown here.

A channel implementation that sends messages unreliably and without ordering guarantees. Suited for time-critical, transient data where latency matters more than reliability (eg. snapshots). It derives from Channel (defined elsewhere). It maintains separate send/receive queues of Message pointers and provides APIs for enqueueing, dequeuing, packetization, and ack processing. Copying is disabled. Construction requires an Allocator, MessageFactory, ChannelConfig, channel index, and initial time.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file only contains function templates and inline/free function declarations and definitions.
Bit-level writer that packs values into a word-aligned buffer in little-endian network order. Requires buffer size multiple of 4. Call FlushBits when done.
Bit-level reader for buffers containing bit-packed values written by BitWriter. Supports unaligned byte sizes; underlying memory must be dword-accessible.
Common base for stream types providing opaque context and allocator pointers for user data and custom allocation.
High-level write stream wrapper over BitWriter with unified serialization API and compile-time IsWriting/IsReading flags.
High-level read stream wrapper over BitReader with unified serialization API and compile-time IsWriting/IsReading flags.
Stream variant that simulates writing to estimate bit and byte counts without producing output. Conservative for alignment.

functions.name: InitializeYojimbo
functions.description: Initializes the Yojimbo networking library. Call this first in your process before using any other Yojimbo APIs. Returns true on successful initialization, false on failure. Typical usage is to check the return value and proceed to create clients/servers only if initialization succeeded.
requirements: Must be called before calling any other Yojimbo library functions.
Caller must check the boolean return value and avoid using Yojimbo if initialization fails.
Should be paired with a later call to ShutdownYojimbo() after finishing with the library (recommended by documentation).

functions.name: EnablePacketTagging
functions.description: Enables DSCP-based packet tagging for all packets sent by Yojimbo, intended to reduce jitter (e.g., on Wi‑Fi 6+ routers). Enable this prior to creating any clients or servers so that tagging is applied to their traffic.
requirements: InitializeYojimbo() must have been successfully called prior to invoking this function (InitializeYojimbo must be called before any Yojimbo functions).
Should be called before creating any client or server instances for tagging to be applied to their packets.

functions.name: ShutdownYojimbo
functions.description: Shuts down the Yojimbo library and performs internal checks (e.g., debug-time leak checks). Call this after you are completely finished using the library.
requirements: InitializeYojimbo() must have been successfully called prior to invoking this function (InitializeYojimbo must be called before any Yojimbo functions).
Call only after you finish using the library (i.e., after you are done with Yojimbo functionality in your process).

functions.name: yojimbo::GetDefaultAllocator

file should identify the calling source file for leak tracking (may be used in diagnostics).

requirements: p must be non-NULL.
p must have been allocated by this same Allocator instance; freeing memory from another allocator or raw malloc will assert/fail.
file and line should correspond to the call site for tracking.

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::Queue
functions.signature: template <typename T> yojimbo::Queue<T>::Queue(Allocator & allocator, int size)
functions.description: Constructs a FIFO circular buffer of capacity size using the provided allocator. Allocates a backing array of T and zero-initializes it. Intended for simple POD-like Ts used in a queue.
requirements: size must be > 0 (asserted)
allocator must remain valid for the lifetime of the Queue instance (the queue stores a pointer to it)
allocator must be able to allocate sizeof(T) * size bytes
T must be trivially default-initializable (backing storage is memset to 0, no constructors are run)
T must be copy-assignable/copyable (elements are assigned and returned by value)

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::~Queue
functions.description: Destructor releases the backing array via the stored allocator and resets internal state. No element destructors are invoked.
requirements: T should not require a destructor to be run when removed or on destruction (storage is freed without invoking T destructors)
The Allocator previously provided must still be valid at destruction time (it is used to free memory)

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::Clear
functions.description: Clears the queue, resetting it to an empty state without freeing memory. Does not destroy or overwrite element storage beyond logical removal.
requirements: T should not require destruction on clear (no destructors are called)

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::Pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the oldest element from the queue. Advances the start index in the circular buffer.
requirements: The queue must not be empty prior to calling (IsEmpty() must be false); otherwise an assertion will trigger
T must be copyable/movable to be returned by value

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::Push
functions.signature: template <typename T> void yojimbo::Queue<T>::Push(const T & value)
functions.description: Appends value to the end of the queue (newest position) if capacity allows. Writes into the circular buffer at the computed tail index.
requirements: The queue must not be full prior to calling (IsFull() must be false); otherwise an assertion will trigger
T must be copy-assignable (value is assigned into internal storage)

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::operator[]
functions.description: Returns a reference to the element at logical position index, where 0 is the oldest element and GetNumEntries()-1 is the newest. Provides random access into the circular buffer.
requirements: The queue must not be empty (IsEmpty() must be false)
index must be >= 0
index must be < GetNumEntries()

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::GetSize
functions.description: Returns the fixed capacity of the queue (maximum number of elements that can be stored).

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::IsFull
functions.description: Returns true if the queue currently holds size elements (ie. it is at full capacity).

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::IsEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if the queue has no elements.

functions.name: yojimbo::Queue::GetNumEntries
functions.description: Returns the current number of elements stored in the queue, in the range [0, GetSize()].

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ReliableOrderedChannel
functions.signature: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ReliableOrderedChannel(Allocator & allocator, MessageFactory & messageFactory, const ChannelConfig & config, int channelIndex, double time)
functions.description: Constructs a reliable, in-order delivery channel for messages. It wires the channel to the allocator and message factory, applies the provided ChannelConfig, assigns a channel index within the connection, and initializes internal timing/state using the supplied time. Use this when creating per-connection channels that guarantee reliable, ordered delivery of messages and support optional block fragmentation.
requirements: allocator must outlive the channel instance.
messageFactory must be valid and outlive the channel instance.
config must be a valid ChannelConfig for a reliable-ordered channel.
channelIndex must be within [0, numChannels-1] for the owning connection (as stated in comments).
time should represent the current connection time and is expected to advance monotonically with AdvanceTime().

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::~ReliableOrderedChannel
functions.description: Destructor. Releases any messages remaining in send/receive queues and tears down internal state (sent packet tracking, block state, etc.). Call when you are done with the channel to clean up resources.
requirements: The channel must not be used after destruction.
All pending operations on the channel should be complete or quiesced before destruction to avoid use-after-free in external code.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::Reset
functions.description: Resets the channel to its initial state. Clears send/receive queues, sent-packet tracking, and block send/receive state. Use to reinitialize a channel without destroying it.
requirements: After Reset(), previously obtained Message* from ReceiveMessage not owned by the channel should already have been consumed by the caller.
Do not use Reset() concurrently with other channel operations.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::CanSendMessage
functions.description: Returns whether a new message can be queued for sending at this time. This considers channel capacity and flow control (eg. not running ahead of receiver). Call before SendMessage().
requirements: No specific input requirements.
If false is returned, caller should not call SendMessage() until later.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::SendMessage
functions.description: Queues a message for reliable, in-order delivery. If the message carries a block, it will be fragmented and sent over multiple packets according to channel configuration. Messages remain in the send queue until individually acked.
requirements: message must be non-null.
message must be allocated/created by the matching MessageFactory associated with this channel.
Caller should check CanSendMessage() before calling to avoid overrun.
context is a user/context pointer passed through for serialization; it may be null if not used by your message types.
Do not free or reuse the message pointer after passing it to SendMessage(); ownership is managed by the channel until the message is acked and released.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ReceiveMessage
functions.description: Dequeues and returns the next fully received message in order, or null if none are available. For block messages, the method returns only after the associated block has been fully reconstructed.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership of the returned Message* and must eventually release/destroy it via the MessageFactory or appropriate API for your integration.
Safe to call repeatedly until it returns null.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::AdvanceTime
functions.description: Advances the channel’s internal time used for resend timers, RTT estimates, and fragment pacing. Call this regularly with the current connection time.
requirements: time should be monotonically non-decreasing relative to prior calls (constructed with an initial time).
Should be called periodically to ensure resend and timeout logic operates correctly.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetPacketData
functions.signature: int yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetPacketData(void * context, ChannelPacketData & packetData, uint16_t packetSequence, int availableBits)
functions.description: Builds channel payload for an outgoing connection packet. Depending on state, it either fills packetData with messages (potentially multiple) or with a single block fragment, and returns an upper-bound estimate of the bits required to serialize it.
requirements: packetData must be a valid reference for output.
availableBits must be >= 0; the channel will respect this as a hard limit.
context is passed through for message serialization and may be null if unused.
packetSequence must be the sequence of the enclosing connection packet.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ProcessPacketData
functions.description: Processes channel data received from a connection packet. Inserts any new messages into the receive queue and processes any block fragment contained in the packet. Tracks per-packet mapping for later ack handling.
requirements: packetData must contain data previously produced by a compatible yojimbo channel.
packetSequence must match the enclosing connection packet’s sequence.
Caller should subsequently call ProcessAck() when the packet is acked to finalize per-message/fragment acks.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ProcessAck
functions.description: Processes an ack for a previously sent connection packet. Uses the per-packet mapping to individually ack contained messages and/or a block fragment, removing them from send tracking.
requirements: ack must be a valid sequence number for a packet previously sent and tracked by this channel.
Should be called when the connection acks a packet that carried this channel’s data.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::HasMessagesToSend
functions.description: Returns true if there is at least one unacked message remaining in the send queue. Messages remain in the send queue until individually acked.
requirements: No input requirements.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetMessagesToSend
functions.signature: int yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetMessagesToSend(uint16_t * messageIds, int & numMessageIds, int remainingPacketBits, void * context)
functions.description: Selects which queued messages to include in the next packet given the remaining bit budget and receiver capacity. Fills messageIds with up to ChannelConfig::maxMessagesPerPacket IDs in send order and returns an upper-bound estimate of the bits required to serialize them.
requirements: messageIds must point to an array sized for at least ChannelConfig::maxMessagesPerPacket entries.
numMessageIds is an output parameter and will be set to the number of IDs written; it must be a valid reference.
remainingPacketBits must be >= 0 and is treated as a hard limit.
context may be null if unused by message serialization.
Caller should call GetMessagePacketData() next with the returned IDs to serialize payload.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetMessagePacketData
functions.signature: void yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetMessagePacketData(ChannelPacketData & packetData, const uint16_t * messageIds, int numMessageIds)
functions.description: Fills packetData with the set of messages identified by messageIds for inclusion in an outgoing packet. Adds references to those messages so they can be tracked until the packet is acked or lost.
requirements: packetData must be a valid output reference.
messageIds must be non-null when numMessageIds > 0 and contain IDs previously returned by GetMessagesToSend().
numMessageIds must be >= 0 and should not exceed ChannelConfig::maxMessagesPerPacket.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::AddMessagePacketEntry
functions.signature: void yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::AddMessagePacketEntry(const uint16_t * messageIds, int numMessageIds, uint16_t sequence)
functions.description: Records a mapping between a sent packet sequence and the set of message IDs included in that packet so that when the packet is acked the messages can be individually acked and released.
requirements: messageIds must be non-null when numMessageIds > 0.
numMessageIds must be >= 0 and should not exceed ChannelConfig::maxMessagesPerPacket.
sequence must be the sequence number of the enclosing connection packet.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ProcessPacketMessages
functions.description: Processes an array of received messages from a packet, inserting any not previously received into the receive queue. Each message added has its reference incremented for queue ownership.
requirements: messages must be non-null when numMessages > 0 and point to an array of Message* of length numMessages.
numMessages must be >= 0.
Messages should be of types valid for this channel/message factory.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::UpdateOldestUnackedMessageId
functions.description: Scans the send queue to update the internal pointer to the oldest unacked message ID, skipping holes caused by individually acked messages. Used as a starting point for message selection for the next packet.
requirements: No input requirements.
Should be called internally before choosing messages to send.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::SendingBlockMessage
functions.description: Returns true if the channel is currently in the mode of sending a block message (ie. still has unacked fragments in flight). In this mode each packet carries exactly one fragment from the current block until all fragments are acked.
requirements: No input requirements.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetFragmentToSend
functions.signature: uint8_t * yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetFragmentToSend(uint16_t & messageId, uint16_t & fragmentId, int & fragmentBytes, int & numFragments, int & messageType)
functions.description: Selects the next block fragment to send by scanning for a fragment that is not yet acked and not recently sent (per fragmentResendTime). Outputs the message and fragment identifiers, size, total number of fragments, and the message type, and returns a pointer to the fragment data.
requirements: Should be called only when SendingBlockMessage() returns true.
Outputs (messageId, fragmentId, fragmentBytes, numFragments, messageType) must be valid lvalue references.
Returned pointer is only valid until the channel state changes; do not retain beyond immediate packet assembly.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetFragmentPacketData
functions.signature: int yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::GetFragmentPacketData(ChannelPacketData & packetData, uint16_t messageId, uint16_t fragmentId, uint8_t * fragmentData, int fragmentSize, int numFragments, int messageType)
functions.description: Fills packetData with a block fragment payload for transmission and returns an upper-bound estimate of the bits needed to serialize it. Used when the channel is sending a block message.
requirements: packetData must be a valid output reference.
fragmentData must be non-null when fragmentSize > 0.
fragmentSize must be >= 0.
fragmentId must be within [0, numFragments-1].
numFragments must be > 0.
messageType must correspond to a message type that allows blocks (as noted in comments).

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::AddFragmentPacketEntry
functions.signature: void yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::AddFragmentPacketEntry(uint16_t messageId, uint16_t fragmentId, uint16_t sequence)
functions.description: Records that a specific fragment of a block (identified by messageId and fragmentId) was included in a connection packet with the given sequence, so that an ack for that packet can ack the fragment.
requirements: fragmentId should be within the valid range for the block [0, numFragments-1].
sequence must be the sequence of the containing connection packet.

functions.name: yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ProcessPacketFragment
functions.signature: void yojimbo::ReliableOrderedChannel::ProcessPacketFragment(int messageType, uint16_t messageId, int numFragments, uint16_t fragmentId, const uint8_t * fragmentData, int fragmentBytes, BlockMessage * blockMessage)
functions.description: Processes a received block fragment. Tracks fragments for the given block and, when all are present, reassembles the block, attaches it to the corresponding block message, and enqueues that message for receive. The first fragment (id 0) may carry the BlockMessage pointer; subsequent fragments pass null.
requirements: messageType must be a message type that allows blocks (per MessageFactory configuration).
messageId identifies the message the block belongs to.
numFragments must be > 0.
fragmentId must be within [0, numFragments-1].
fragmentData must be non-null when fragmentBytes > 0.
fragmentBytes must be >= 0.
blockMessage must be provided (non-null) only with the first fragment (fragmentId == 0); pass NULL for all other fragments as stated in comments.

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::SequenceBuffer
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::SequenceBuffer( yojimbo::Allocator & allocator, int size )
functions.description: Constructs a sequence buffer that stores entries indexed by 16-bit sequence numbers with constant-time lookup by sequence modulo buffer size. Allocates internal arrays for sequence tags and entries using the provided allocator. Typical usage: create one buffer per stream (eg. packet acks, reliable queues) with a fixed capacity, then Insert entries as sequences arrive.
requirements: size must be > 0 (asserted)
allocator must remain valid for the lifetime of the SequenceBuffer (used for allocation and deallocation)
Sufficient memory must be available in allocator to allocate sizeof(uint32_t)*size and sizeof(T)*size; construction will assert/assume success
After construction, buffer is reset to empty state

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::~SequenceBuffer
functions.description: Destructs the sequence buffer and frees internal storage for entries and sequence tags via the allocator provided at construction.
requirements: allocator must still be valid at destruction time (used for freeing)
All pointers returned by Insert are invalidated upon destruction; callers must not retain or use them afterward

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Reset
functions.description: Clears the buffer to its initial empty state: advances internal most-recent sequence to 0 and marks all slots as unoccupied. Use to reinitialize the buffer without destroying it.
requirements: After Reset, any previously obtained entry pointers are invalid and must not be used
Can be called at any time; no arguments required

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Insert
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T * yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Insert( uint16_t sequence, bool guaranteed_order = false )
functions.description: Inserts or assigns the slot for the given sequence number and returns a pointer to the entry to be filled by the caller. If the sequence is too old (outside the buffer window), returns NULL. If another entry exists at the same index (sequence % size), it is overwritten. When guaranteed_order is true (eg. for sending), or sequence+1 is newer than the current most-recent sequence, the buffer advances and old entries in the advanced range are cleared.
requirements: Caller must check for and handle a NULL return, which indicates the sequence is too old to be inserted
Caller must populate the returned entry pointer with their data before further operations that may overwrite it
be aware that inserting may overwrite an existing entry at (sequence % size) regardless of whether an entry for a different sequence occupied that slot
If guaranteed_order is true, caller guarantees sequences are non-decreasing; function will clear intervening entries accordingly
Sequence values are 16-bit and wrap; relative ordering follows yojimbo_sequence_greater_than/less_than semantics

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Remove
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
void yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Remove( uint16_t sequence )
functions.description: Marks the entry corresponding to the given sequence number as unoccupied (if present) by clearing its slot.
requirements: Safe to call even if no entry exists for the given sequence; it will simply clear the slot
Sequence is treated modulo the buffer size; removing a sequence clears the slot at index (sequence % size)

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Available
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Available( uint16_t sequence ) const
functions.description: Checks whether the slot corresponding to the given sequence number is currently unoccupied and available for insertion.
requirements: Returns true if slot at (sequence % size) is marked as empty; does not verify that the slot belongs to the exact sequence beyond emptiness
Pure query; no side effects

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Exists
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Exists( uint16_t sequence ) const
functions.description: Returns true if an entry for the exact sequence number currently exists in the buffer (not just that the slot is occupied).
requirements: Sequence comparison is exact against stored sequence tag; uses (sequence % size) to locate slot
Pure query; no side effects

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Find
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T * yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Find( uint16_t sequence )
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the entry for the given sequence number if it exists; otherwise returns NULL.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL before dereferencing
Returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent Insert/Reset/destruction or by a later Insert that overwrites the same index

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::Find
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const T * yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::Find( uint16_t sequence ) const
functions.description: Const-qualified lookup of an entry by sequence number. Returns a const pointer if the entry exists, otherwise NULL.
requirements: Caller must check for NULL before dereferencing
Pointer remains valid only until the buffer is modified (eg. Insert/Remove/Reset/destruction)

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::GetAtIndex
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T * yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::GetAtIndex( int index )
functions.description: Returns the entry at the specified buffer index if occupied, otherwise NULL. Useful for iterating across underlying slots without sequence translation.
requirements: index must be in range [0, GetSize()-1] (asserted)
Caller must check for NULL before use
Returned pointer may be invalidated by subsequent Insert/Remove/Reset/destruction

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::GetAtIndex
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
const T * yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::GetAtIndex( int index ) const
functions.description: Const-qualified access to the entry at a specific buffer index if occupied; otherwise returns NULL. Supports read-only iteration across slots.
requirements: index must be in range [0, GetSize()-1] (asserted)
Caller must check for NULL before use
Pointer remains valid only until the buffer is modified (eg. Insert/Remove/Reset/destruction)

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::GetSequence
functions.description: Returns the most recent sequence number considered by the buffer. This value advances when inserting newer sequences and wraps at 16-bit boundaries.
requirements: Pure query; no side effects
Interpretation of recency must consider 16-bit wrap semantics used by yojimbo_sequence_greater_than/less_than

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::GetIndex
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
int yojimbo::SequenceBuffer<T>::GetIndex( uint16_t sequence ) const
functions.description: Computes the buffer index for a given sequence number as sequence % size.
requirements: Pure query; no side effects
Valid only when size > 0 (guaranteed by construction)

functions.name: yojimbo::SequenceBuffer::GetSize
functions.description: Returns the fixed capacity (number of slots) of the sequence buffer.
requirements: Pure query; no side effects

functions.name: yojimbo::serialize_ack_relative_internal
functions.signature:
template <typename Stream>
bool yojimbo::serialize_ack_relative_internal(Stream & stream, uint16_t sequence, uint16_t & ack)
functions.description: Serializes an acknowledgment sequence number relative to the current 16-bit sequence number. When writing, it encodes the ack either as a small delta (if within a short range) or as a full 16-bit value; when reading, it decodes and writes the result into ack. Intended for use inside templated serialize functions that operate over read/write/measure stream types.
requirements: Stream must be a compatible Yojimbo stream type that exposes static flags Stream::IsWriting and Stream::IsReading and works with serialize_bool, serialize_int, and serialize_bits utility functions in scope.
sequence is a 16-bit sequence number representing the current sequence.
When Stream::IsWriting is true, ack must be a valid 16-bit sequence number to be encoded; when Stream::IsReading is true, ack is an output parameter that will be assigned the decoded sequence.
Caller must ensure the appropriate serialize_* helpers are available and that stream is in a valid state for the operation.

functions.name: yojimbo::serialize_sequence_relative_internal
functions.signature:
template <typename Stream>
bool yojimbo::serialize_sequence_relative_internal(Stream & stream, uint16_t sequence1, uint16_t & sequence2)
functions.description: Serializes sequence2 relative to sequence1 for 16-bit sequence numbers. When writing, it encodes sequence2 as a value relative to sequence1; when reading, it decodes and writes the resulting 16-bit sequence into sequence2, handling wrap-around.
requirements: Stream must be a compatible Yojimbo stream type that exposes static flags Stream::IsWriting and Stream::IsReading and works with serialize_int_relative helper in scope.
sequence1 and sequence2 are 16-bit sequence numbers; on read, sequence2 is an output parameter and will be assigned.
Caller must ensure the appropriate serialize_* helpers are available and that stream is in a valid state for the operation.

functions.name: yojimbo::Serializable::SerializeInternal
functions.description: Pure virtual serialize function for reading. Implementations must read the object’s state from the provided ReadStream and return true on success or false on failure. Typically overridden via YOJIMBO_VIRTUAL_SERIALIZE_FUNCTIONS to forward to a templated Serialize method.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes (pure virtual).
stream must be a valid yojimbo::ReadStream positioned for reading the object’s data.
Return value must indicate success (true) or failure (false).

functions.name: yojimbo::Serializable::SerializeInternal
functions.description: Pure virtual serialize function for writing. Implementations must write the object’s state to the provided WriteStream and return true on success or false on failure. Commonly provided via YOJIMBO_VIRTUAL_SERIALIZE_FUNCTIONS to call a templated Serialize method.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes (pure virtual).
stream must be a valid yojimbo::WriteStream ready to accept the object’s data.
Return value must indicate success (true) or failure (false).

functions.name: yojimbo::Serializable::SerializeInternal
functions.description: Pure virtual serialize function for measuring. Implementations must update the MeasureStream to reflect how many bits the object would consume if written, and return true on success or false on failure. Often supplied via YOJIMBO_VIRTUAL_SERIALIZE_FUNCTIONS to call a templated Serialize method.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes (pure virtual).
stream must be a valid yojimbo::MeasureStream used to measure the bit size of the object’s serialized form.
Return value must indicate success (true) or failure (false).

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::Server
functions.signature: yojimbo::Server::Server(yojimbo::Allocator & allocator, const uint8_t privateKey[], const yojimbo::Address & address, const yojimbo::ClientServerConfig & config, yojimbo::Adapter & adapter, double time)
functions.description: Constructs a server instance using the provided allocator, private key, bind address, configuration, adapter, and initial time. Intended to set up internal state prior to Start().
requirements: allocator must outlive the Server instance (inferred from reference parameter)
privateKey must point to a buffer containing KeyBytes bytes (inferred from member m_privateKey[KeyBytes])
address is the desired bind address; actual bound address may differ (eg. ephemeral port)
config and adapter must outlive the Server instance (inferred from reference parameters)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::~Server
functions.description: Destroys the server instance, releasing any resources acquired by the server (sockets, memory, etc.). Should be called after Stop() and after any outstanding operations complete.
requirements: Ensure Stop() has been called before destruction if the server was started (inferred best practice)
Do not use the server object after the destructor completes

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::Start
functions.description: Starts the server, binding to its configured address and preparing it to accept and service up to maxClients connections.
requirements: Call only once per server lifetime before Stop(), or call Stop() before starting again (inferred from typical lifecycle)
maxClients should be a non-negative integer; zero may start a server that accepts no clients (inferred from naming)
Must be called before calling SendPackets(), ReceivePackets(), or accepting clients (inferred from typical usage)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::Stop
functions.description: Stops the server, closing network resources and disconnecting clients as needed. After Stop(), the server is no longer processing or accepting network traffic.
requirements: May be called after Start(); calling Stop() when not started should be a no-op (inferred)
After Stop(), do not call SendPackets()/ReceivePackets() until Start() is called again (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::DisconnectClient
functions.description: Forcibly disconnects the client at the specified index from the server.
requirements: clientIndex must refer to a valid client slot created by Start(maxClients) (inferred)
Server should be started when calling this function (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::DisconnectAllClients
functions.description: Disconnects all currently connected clients from the server.
requirements: Server should be started when calling this function (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::SendPackets
functions.description: Sends any pending outbound packets to clients. Typically called once per tick/frame.
requirements: Server must be started (inferred)
Should be called periodically in the server update loop (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::ReceivePackets
functions.description: Processes inbound packets from clients. Typically called once per tick/frame to service the network.
requirements: Server must be started (inferred)
Should be called periodically in the server update loop (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::AdvanceTime
functions.description: Advances the server’s internal time to the provided absolute time value. Used to drive time-based networking logic.
requirements: time should be monotonically non-decreasing relative to previous calls, starting from the constructor’s initial time (inferred from naming and common pattern)
Should be called regularly to keep the server’s time in sync (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::IsClientConnected
functions.description: Returns whether the client at the given index is currently connected.
requirements: clientIndex must refer to a valid client slot (inferred)
Server should be started or have knowledge of client state (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::GetClientId
functions.description: Retrieves the unique 64-bit identifier for the client at the specified index.

The client should be connected for the ID to be meaningful; behavior for disconnected clients is unspecified (unknown)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::GetClientUserData
functions.description: Returns a pointer to user data associated with the client at the given index, if any. The size/format of the data is not specified in this header.
requirements: clientIndex must refer to a valid client slot (inferred)
Returned pointer may be null if no user data is present (unknown; not specified)
Do not modify the returned data (const-qualified)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::GetClientAddress
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the network address for the client at the specified index.

The returned pointer must not be used after the client disconnects or the server stops (inferred)

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::GetNumConnectedClients
functions.description: Returns the number of clients currently connected to the server.

functions.name: yojimbo::Server::ConnectLoopbackClient
functions.signature: void yojimbo::Server::ConnectLoopbackClient(int clientIndex, uint64_t clientId, const uint8_t * userData)
functions.description: Connects a loopback client (local in-process client) to the server at the given index with the specified clientId and optional userData.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate interesting, but valid, byte buffers that will be consumed
# by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME in the provided stubs. Those stubs
# use strings as:
# - file path / file name arguments (Allocator Allocate/Free bookkeeping)
# - printf-like format string arguments (yojimbo_printf)
# - generic textual data for serialization/copy helpers
#
# Therefore, we produce a corpus entry containing multiple concatenated C-strings
# (each NUL-terminated) so the fuzzer runtime can split them into std::string
# instances as needed. The content set mixes:
# - ASCII, whitespace, punctuation, long/short strings
# - Path-like forms (POSIX and Windows)
# - Format strings with various specifiers (safe and matched in stubs)
# - Edge cases: empty, very long near limits, high-bit UTF-8 bytes
# - Repeated and similar names to exercise dedup and caching paths
#
# Size is kept <= 4096 bytes.

SAFE_FORMATS = [
    b"fuzz literal log\n",
    b"%s\n",
    b"%d\n",
    b"%u %u\n",
    b"val=%d str=%s\n",
]

POSIX_PATHS = [
    b"/tmp/fuzz.bin",
    b"/var/log/yojimbo.log",
    b"./relative/path/file.txt",
    b"../up/one/dir.dat",
    b"/dev/null",
]

WIN_PATHS = [
    b"C:\\Temp\\fuzz.bin",
    b"D:\\logs\\yojimbo.log",
    b"..\\relative\\file.txt",
    b"\\\\server\\share\\file.bin",
]

TEXT_SNIPPETS = [
    b"hello",
    b"alloc.c",
    b"allocator.cpp",
    b"main.cc",
    b"unit_test.cpp",
    b"y.cpp",
    b"a.c",
    b"x.h",
    b"readme.md",
]

# Some UTF-8-ish bytes to stress handling but still valid as std::string content
UTF8_CHUNKS = [
    "\u2603 snowman".encode("utf-8"),
    "na\u00EFve caf\u00E9".encode("utf-8"),
    "汉字/漢字".encode("utf-8"),
    "emoji 😺".encode("utf-8"),
]

# Generate a random component for variability, avoiding embedded NULs.

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    population = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:/\\[](){}#@!+%~,;^$&'`"
    return "".join(rng.choice(population) for _ in range(length)).encode("utf-8")


def _cstr(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no interior NULs; append terminating NUL
    return b.replace(b"\x00", b"?") + b"\x00"


def _bounded_repeat(parts: List[bytes], limit: int) -> List[bytes]:
    out = []
    total = 0
    for p in parts:
        if total + len(p) <= limit:
            out.append(p)
            total += len(p)
        else:
            break
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Include several safe printf formats used by yojimbo_printf stub
    fmt_variants = SAFE_FORMATS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(fmt_variants)
    parts.extend(_cstr(f) for f in fmt_variants)

    # 2) Include a variety of file names and paths for Allocate/Free bookkeeping
    paths = POSIX_PATHS + WIN_PATHS
    rng.shuffle(paths)
    parts.extend(_cstr(p) for p in paths[:rng.randint(3, len(paths))])

    # 3) Common source-like filenames that may appear in file/line parameters
    rng.shuffle(TEXT_SNIPPETS)
    parts.extend(_cstr(s) for s in TEXT_SNIPPETS[:rng.randint(3, len(TEXT_SNIPPETS))])

    # 4) UTF-8 content to exercise string copying/serialization
    utf = UTF8_CHUNKS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(utf)
    parts.extend(_cstr(u) for u in utf[:rng.randint(1, len(utf))])

    # 5) Edge cases: empty string, single-char, long strings
    parts.append(_cstr(b""))
    parts.append(_cstr(b"a"))
    parts.append(_cstr(b"0"))

    long1 = _rand_ascii(rng, 64, 256)
    long2 = _rand_ascii(rng, 257, 512)
    parts.append(_cstr(long1))
    parts.append(_cstr(long2))

    # 6) Random extra strings to increase diversity
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)):
        parts.append(_cstr(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 64)))

    # 7) A couple of format-like but safe strings to test non-used specifiers
    parts.append(_cstr(b"%x %08x"))
    parts.append(_cstr(b"%lld %zu %p"))

    # 8) Ensure overall size <= 4096
    combined = b"".join(_bounded_repeat(parts, 4096))
    # If somehow empty, provide at least one NUL
    if not combined:
        combined = b"\x00"
    return combined

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List

# Generator for arbitrary binary blobs tailored to yojimbo fuzz stubs that expect:
# - Serialized ChannelPacketData via serialize::{Read,Write,Measure}Stream
# - Packet payloads for loopback processing (client/server)
# - NetworkSimulator packets
# - Connect tokens and private keys (opaque)
#
# Strategy:
# Produce a bytes buffer comprised of one of several profiles chosen by seed:
# 1) Bit-packed looking data (aligned to 4 bytes) to satisfy BitReader/Writer preconditions.
# 2) Length-prefixed message-like segments with alignment padding.
# 3) Realistic packet-sized payload (<= 1200 bytes) for loopback paths.
# 4) Opaque key/token buffers (64..512 bytes) for Client::Connect/InsecureConnect and Server ctor.
# 5) Block fragment-like sequences mixing varying sizes to exercise fragment handling paths.
# All buffers remain valid arbitrary blobs (no mutations post build) and size <= 4096.

_MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_ipv4(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return bytes([rng.randrange(1, 255) for _ in range(4)])

def _align4(b: bytearray) -> None:
    pad = (-len(b)) & 3
    if pad:
        b.extend(b"\x00" * pad)

def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    return zlib.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF

def _bitpacked_blob(rng: random.Random, target_bytes: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose fields with explicit bit widths then pack into 32-bit words.
    words: List[int] = []
    remaining = max(1, target_bytes // 4)
    for _ in range(remaining):
        flags = rng.getrandbits(8)
        a = rng.getrandbits(10)
        b = rng.getrandbits(5)
        c = rng.getrandbits(9)
        d = rng.getrandbits(32)
        w = ((flags & 0xFF) << 24) ^ ((a & 0x3FF) << 14) ^ ((b & 0x1F) << 9) ^ ((c & 0x1FF))
        w ^= (d & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        words.append(w & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    blob = bytearray()
    for w in words:
        blob.extend(struct.pack('<I', w))
    # Ensure size exactly target_bytes (pad or trim)
    if len(blob) < target_bytes:
        blob.extend(os.urandom(target_bytes - len(blob)))
    elif len(blob) > target_bytes:
        del blob[target_bytes:]
    return bytes(blob)

def _length_prefixed_segments(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a sequence of [len][payload][align] segments with varied payload kinds
    out = bytearray()
    alpha = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"
    while len(out) + 8 < budget:
        kind = rng.randrange(0, 4)
        if kind == 0:
            # small textual-ish
            size = rng.randint(1, min(64, max(1, budget - len(out) - 8)))
            payload = bytearray(alpha[rng.randrange(0, len(alpha))] for _ in range(size))
        elif kind == 1:
            # random bytes
            size = rng.randint(1, min(256, max(1, budget - len(out) - 8)))
            payload = bytearray(os.urandom(size))
        elif kind == 2:
            # repeated pattern
            if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes'):
                base = rng.randbytes(4)
            else:
                base = os.urandom(4)
            reps = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(64, (budget - len(out) - 8) // 4)))
            payload = bytearray(base * reps)
        else:
            # embedded ipv4 + port
            payload = bytearray()
            payload.extend(_rand_ipv4(rng))
            payload.extend(struct.pack('<H', rng.randrange(0, 65536)))
        # length prefix (little endian)
        out.extend(struct.pack('<I', len(payload)))
        out.extend(payload)
        _align4(out)
    return bytes(out)

def _packet_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a realistic packet: header + body + checksum, <= 1200 bytes
    mtu = rng.randint(64, 1200)
    body_budget = max(0, mtu - 12)  # 4 magic + 4 seq + 4 crc
    body = _length_prefixed_segments(rng, body_budget)
    magic = b'YJMB'
    seq = rng.getrandbits(32)
    header = magic + struct.pack('<I', seq)
    crc = struct.pack('<I', _crc32(body))
    pkt = header + body + crc
    # ensure <= 1200 and multiple of 4 to please BitReader
    pkt = pkt[:mtu]
    if len(pkt) % 4 != 0:
        pkt += b"\x00" * (-len(pkt) & 3)
    return pkt

def _opaque_key_or_token(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 64..512 bytes of random data, multiple of 4
    size = rng.randrange(64, 513)
    size = (size + 3) & ~3
    data = bytearray(os.urandom(size))
    # sprinkle some structure: put a crc at the end and a version at start
    if size >= 12:
        version = rng.randrange(0, 5)
        data[0:4] = struct.pack('<I', version)
        crc = zlib.crc32(data[:-4]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
        data[-4:] = struct.pack('<I', crc)
    return bytes(data)

def _block_fragment_like(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose a series of small fragments: [numFrags][for each: id,len,data(padded)]
    out = bytearray()
    num = rng.randint(1, 8)
    out.extend(struct.pack('<I', num))
    for frag_id in range(num):
        frag_len = rng.randint(1, 512)
        data = os.urandom(frag_len)
        out.extend(struct.pack('<H', frag_id))
        out.extend(struct.pack('<H', frag_len))
        out.extend(data)
        _align4(out)
    # cap size
    if len(out) > 1500:
        out = bytearray(out[:1500])
        _align4(out)
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a profile
    profile = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if profile == 0:
        # Bit-packed blob aiming for 512..2048 bytes and multiple of 4
        size = rng.randrange(512, 2049)
        size = (size + 3) & ~3
        return _bitpacked_blob(rng, size)
    elif profile == 1:
        # Length-prefixed segments up to ~2KB
        budget = rng.randrange(256, 2048)
        blob = _length_prefixed_segments(rng, budget)
        if len(blob) == 0:
            blob = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
        return blob[:_MAX_BYTES]
    elif profile == 2:
        # Realistic packet payload
        return _packet_payload(rng)
    elif profile == 3:
        # Opaque key or token buffer
        return _opaque_key_or_token(rng)
    elif profile == 4:
        # Block fragment like buffer
        return _block_fragment_like(rng)
    else:
        # Mixed: concatenate a small packet with a small token, keep under limit
        pkt = _packet_payload(rng)
        tok = _opaque_key_or_token(rng)
        out = bytearray()
        out.extend(struct.pack('<I', len(pkt)))
        out.extend(pkt)
        _align4(out)
        tok_part = tok[:max(32, 256)]
        out.extend(struct.pack('<I', len(tok_part)))
        out.extend(tok_part)
        _align4(out)
        return bytes(out[:_MAX_BYTES])
